quizzes.title: Dad Joke Showdown
quizzes.description: Classic groan-worthy punchlines. Points for the right answer, extra respect for the loudest groan.

questions.q: What do you call a fish with no eyes?
questions.note: Take the i's out of fish and you're left with a fsh.

questions.q: Why don't skeletons fight each other?
questions.note: No guts, no glory, and no fights either.

questions.q: What do you call a bear with no teeth?
questions.note: Gummy: no teeth, all gums.

questions.q: Why did the scarecrow win an award?
options: He was outstanding in his field
questions.note: He stands in a field, and he's outstanding; that's the whole joke.

questions.q: The answer to 'What do you call a sleeping bull?' is 'a cowboy'.
questions.note: It's a bulldozer: a bull that dozes.

questions.q: What do you call a dinosaur that's fast asleep?
questions.note: Dinosaur, dino-snore; say it out loud for full effect.

questions.q: What do you call a cow with no legs?
questions.note: It's on the ground, and it's beef.

questions.q: The answer to 'Why can't a bicycle stand up on its own?' is 'because it's two-tired'.
questions.note: Two tyres, too tired.

questions.q: What did the ocean say to the beach?
questions.note: Accept any answer with "waved"; waves are how the sea says hello.

questions.q: What do you call a big pile of cats?
questions.note: Accept "meowtain" or anything close; a mountain of meows.

quizzes.title: Animal Antics
quizzes.description: Cube-shaped poo, hand-holding otters and pebble proposals: the animal kingdom is ridiculous.

questions.q: What shape is wombat poo?
questions.note: Wombats leave cube-shaped droppings, which don't roll away from the rocks they use to mark territory.

questions.q: Which animal often holds paws while sleeping so it doesn't drift away?
questions.note: Sea otters float on their backs and hold on to each other or wrap themselves in kelp.

questions.q: Why are flamingos pink?
questions.note: Pigments in the algae and brine shrimp they eat turn them pink; chicks hatch grey.

questions.q: A group of flamingos is called a 'flamboyance'.
questions.note: Fitting for a bird that stands on one leg in bright pink.

questions.q: What is a baby puffin called?
questions.note: Pufflings hatch in burrows and stay hidden for about six weeks.

questions.q: Which bird can fly backwards?
questions.note: Hummingbirds can hover, fly backwards and even briefly upside down.

questions.q: Which animal has fingerprints so like ours they could confuse a crime scene?
questions.note: Koala fingerprints have loops and whorls that look very like human ones.

questions.q: An octopus has three hearts.
questions.note: Two pump blood through the gills and one through the rest of the body; its blood is blue too.

questions.q: Which slow, plant-eating sea mammal is nicknamed the 'sea cow'?
questions.note: Also accept dugong; sailors may have mistaken them for mermaids.

questions.q: Which bird do gentoo males 'propose' to by offering a pebble?
questions.note: Gentoo and Adélie penguins use pebbles to build nests, so a good stone is a serious gift.

quizzes.title: Weird but True
quizzes.description: Unicorns, radioactive bananas and a war that ended before lunch. All of it true.

questions.q: What colour is a polar bear's skin?
questions.note: Black skin soaks up heat; the fur is see-through, not white.

questions.q: What is the national animal of Scotland?
questions.note: The unicorn has been a Scottish royal symbol for centuries and still appears on the royal coat of arms.

questions.q: Bananas are very slightly radioactive.
questions.note: They contain potassium, a tiny part of which is radioactive potassium-40; perfectly safe to eat.

questions.q: Which country has more ancient pyramids than Egypt?
questions.note: Sudan has around 200 Nubian pyramids, smaller and steeper than Egypt's.

questions.q: The designer of which snack's tube had some of his ashes buried in one?
questions.note: Fredric Baur designed the Pringles can, and his family honoured his wish in 2008.

questions.q: Roughly how long did the Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896, the shortest war on record, last?
questions.note: Estimates range from 38 to 45 minutes.

questions.q: Honey found in ancient Egyptian tombs was still edible thousands of years later.
questions.note: Honey is so low in water and so acidic that microbes can't grow in it.

questions.q: On which planet is a day longer than its year?
questions.note: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once but only about 225 to orbit the Sun.

questions.q: What is the small dot over a lowercase i or j called?
questions.note: Every i and j you have ever written has a tittle.

questions.q: What's the name for the plastic tip on the end of a shoelace?
questions.note: Aglets stop laces fraying and make them easier to thread.

quizzes.title: Silly History
quizzes.description: Wars lost to birds, a flood of syrup and a town that couldn't stop dancing.

questions.q: In 1932 Australia's army fought a 'war' against which animal, and lost?
questions.note: Soldiers with machine guns couldn't stop the fast, scattering emus from eating the wheat crops.

questions.q: In the 1830s, tomato ketchup was sold in America as a…
questions.note: Tomato pills and extracts were sold as cures for indigestion and more.

questions.q: In industrial Britain, who woke workers by tapping on windows with a long pole?
questions.note: Knocker-uppers were paid a few pence a week to be the alarm clock.

questions.q: In 1518, people in Strasbourg couldn't stop doing what for weeks?
questions.note: The 'dancing plague' drew in dozens of people, perhaps hundreds; nobody knows exactly why.

questions.q: In 1919, a wave of molasses flooded the streets of which city?
questions.note: A huge tank burst and a sticky wave several metres high swept through the North End.

questions.q: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
questions.note: The Great Pyramid is about 2,500 years older than her; the Moon landing came about 2,000 years after.

questions.q: Before rubber erasers, what did people often use to rub out pencil marks?
questions.note: Balled-up bread crumbs did the job until rubber took over in the 1770s.

questions.q: The Roman emperor Vespasian put a tax on collecting urine from public toilets.
questions.note: Urine was used for laundry and tanning; 'pecunia non olet', money doesn't stink.

questions.q: Which 18th-century earl lent his name to a lunchtime favourite?
questions.note: Accept "Earl of Sandwich"; John Montagu supposedly wanted food he could eat without leaving his cards.

questions.q: Which stretchy one-piece garment is named after French acrobat Jules?
questions.note: Jules Léotard, the original 'daring young man on the flying trapeze', made it popular.

quizzes.title: Oddities & Odd Words
quizzes.description: Petrichor, philtrums and a fear of long words. A tricky one for the know-it-alls.

questions.q: Which letter doesn't appear in the name of any US state?
questions.note: J is in New Jersey, Z in Arizona and X in Texas, but no state has a Q.

questions.q: What is 'petrichor'?
options: The smell of rain on dry ground
questions.note: The earthy smell comes partly from oils released by plants and a chemical made by soil bacteria.

questions.q: A group of which birds is called a 'parliament'?
questions.note: A group of crows, meanwhile, is a 'murder'.

questions.q: Which cartoonist coined 'anatidaephobia', the fear that a duck is watching you?
questions.note: It comes from a 'Far Side' cartoon; it isn't a real medical condition.

questions.q: What is the name of the moustached mascot of the board game Monopoly?
questions.note: He's now officially called Mr. Monopoly.

questions.q: What does someone with 'hippopotomonstrosesquippedaliophobia' fear?
questions.note: Making the name that long is either a joke or very cruel.

questions.q: The Eiffel Tower can grow more than 10 cm taller on a hot summer day.
questions.note: Its iron expands in the heat; the top can rise by up to about 15 cm.

questions.q: A sloth can hold its breath longer than a dolphin.
questions.note: By slowing its heart, a sloth can last about 40 minutes underwater; dolphins usually surface every few minutes.

questions.q: Apart from 'hash' or 'pound', what is the # symbol called?
questions.note: Accept "octothorp"; the name was made up at Bell Labs in the 1960s.

questions.q: What is the groove between your nose and your upper lip called?
questions.note: Most people can't name it, but everyone has one.
